correctness.rationale: In order-only reflexive-poset language, C^2 can count predecessors/successors and block type cardinalities. For B_n degrees (2^r-1,2^(n-r)-1) identify rank r; for n=3 rank sizes 1,3,3,1 and strict comparison counts force a 2-regular simple bipartite 3+3 graph, uniquely a 6-cycle (complement of a perfect matching). n<=2 is forced by degrees. At n=4 construct T with rank sizes 1,4,6,4,1, three copies each of middle supports {1,2} and {3,4}, other supports canonical; partial order via support inclusion across strata. Its all ordered atomic-type block degree counts match B4, hence C^2-equivalent by one-variable counting color refinement, but two atoms have three incomparable minimal upper bounds/no join. Product preserving colored-type counts extends to T×B_{n-4} for every n>=4; no such product is lattice. Independent 16-point block profile and three-minimal-upper-bound checks passed; packaged programs cover n<=8 only, proof gives all n.
residual_risks: Independent n=4 finite check supports but does not establish C2 preservation for arbitrary product dimension; inspected proof does.

value.rationale: Boolean lattices are canonical finite posets; identification by the very weak but expressive C^2 with counting in the order-only signature is an intrinsically motivated recognition boundary. The 16-element nonlattice competitor and its all-dimensional product propagation rigorously explain a stable limitation of two-variable refinement, not a small unmotivated census.
residual_risks: Scope boundary: Competitors Q_n are finite posets but not lattices; no claim about C2 among lattices/distributive lattices, or with named Boolean operations and constants.
